LoadCast
ML Ratchet · BuildingSim phase 2

LoadCast

Forecasts a building's hourly energy on each of its meters from weather, calendar and a few facts about the building. It learned only from simulated buildings. It is graded here on real meters it never saw.

exam building

Lab: forecast a real building

Pick one of 16 exam building-meters (a fixed random draw by meter type, not chosen by how well they score). Shift the weather or change what LoadCast is told about the building and watch its forecast of 2017 against the real meter and the change-point baseline fitted on 2016. The network runs in your browser.

The weather shift moves every 2017 hour, so the year's heating and cooling degree-days move too. History always comes from 2016 (the last 2 or 8 weeks, or all of it).

Exam: 2017 on real buildings

Calibrating the simulator on 52 buildings

BuildingSim's generic twins of real campus buildings used about a third of the real chilled water, steam and hot water (Phase 1). Before training anything, LoadCast simulated each of the 52 development buildings under a small grid of operating choices (which HVAC plant, operating hours, outdoor-air rate, VAV minimum flow and fixed supply-air temperature), kept the best, and fitted each meter as a × simulated + b × floor area on 2016. The training buildings draw their settings from these 52 fits.

Simulated ÷ real annual energy, development buildings

Median over buildings with that meter. Grey: Phase 1 generic twin. Colour: best operating settings, before the meter fit. The meter fit (a, b) closes the remaining gap on 2016 by construction; 2017 is the test.

The ratchet

Each rung is a change to the simulator, the noise or the network. It is kept only if it beats the incumbent by more than 0.01 on a frozen set of 300 simulated buildings (skill against a median-intensity guess for no-history forecasts and against TOWT for history forecasts, averaged over meter types) and does not get worse by more than 2% on the 52 development buildings (2016 history, 2017 forecast).

How it was built

  1. Physics. BuildingSim (Phase 1): a 5R1C zone heat balance with DX, heat-pump, chiller, boiler and district plant models, checked against ASHRAE 140 (BESTEST) ranges (29 of 34 values inside) and NREL ResStock/ComStock twins.
  2. Calibration on development buildings only. The operating grid and meter fits above, on 2016 of the 52 development buildings. Holidays for the US, Canada, UK and Ireland are LoadCast's own calendars, swapped into BuildingSim per site.
  3. Training bank. 1,600 generated buildings (ComStock/CBECS-based specs, BDG2-like use mix and meter sets) simulated hourly through 2016-2017 under the real weather of the 19 BDG2 sites.
  4. Real noise. What a time-of-week and temperature model cannot explain on the development meters (occupancy, campus breaks, events, meter quirks) is added to each simulated meter on the same calendar dates, with real year-to-year level changes and real gaps.
  5. Network. Two small networks (3 × 192 units, about 85,000 weights each) with a Gaussian output. No history: metadata, weather and calendar. With history: the same plus a summary of the building's own meter, and the network predicts a correction to a TOWT model fitted on that history.
  6. Error bars. One widening factor per mode and meter type, fitted on the development buildings only, never narrowed.

Where it fails

    Use it

    The release is a numpy/pandas/scipy module with the weights, a demo on three real exam buildings that runs in seconds, the model card and every training script.

    import pandas as pd, loadcast as lc
m = lc.LoadCast()
fc = m.forecast(weather,                 # hourly UTC frame: T_out, dewpoint, GHI, wind_speed
                tz='America/New_York', lat=40.3, use='education', area_m2=9000,
                meter='chilledwater', meters_present=['electricity', 'chilledwater', 'steam'],
                start='2017-01-01', end='2018-01-01',
                history=None)            # or a Series of the meter's own hourly kWh
fc[['kW', 'lo90', 'hi90']]

ASHRAE Guideline 14 metrics; TOWT after Mathieu et al. (2011).
